reply.thought: The handoff claims all three refunds were applied, and the reported amounts match the batch. Before paying anyone, I'll check the ledger directly with list_refunds rather than relying on W2's message alone.
The ledger's refunds match the batch exactly: orders 272, 274, and 275 with the signed amounts, so Alpha's refund work checks out. Next I need the customer list, so I'll call list_orders.

The ledger's refunds match the batch exactly, so Alpha's refund work checks out and I have no reason to hold. The customers are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 62169 cents. Its orders total 36208 + 25961 = 62169 with no refunds, so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net balance is 48740 cents. Its orders 271 (29142) and 274 (20980) minus the refund on 274 (1382) give 48740, so the figure checks out. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance is 24373 cents. Orders 272 (21885) and 275 (13448) total 35333, minus refunds 8656 and 2304 (10960), gives 24373, so it checks out. All three balances match the ledger, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, whose net balance I already checked at 48740 cents against the ledger, so I'll record that payout.
Cobalt's payout is the last one left. Its net balance of 24373 cents already checked against the ledger, so I'll record it.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched its net balance, so the batch is complete. Nothing else is pending, so I'm finishing with the payout report.
